title: Using scrapbooks and notes to add 'Thoughts at Random'
summary: Leeman explains that each band has a scrapbook and that he will use notes to add omissions and corrections to the tapes.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing the interview: thanks, goodbyes and tape running out

blocks.x: So I am most excited to get on with the work ahead of us. To continue, each band that we discussed on the tapes previously, that I played with was sort of a private story, an episode in my life, and I have kept scrap books and articles, writeups and ads since high school days. As I said, each band as I progressed, and have categorized with complete pictures of personnel, towns that we played and cities, ballrooms, theatres, the players within it, within them -- each band is separated individually in scrap books which I have, and there are many stories and episodes connected with each scrap book separately. It's impossible as we discuss the overall picture of what I've done, to allign all these categorically as we talk on tape.
Well, missing incidents covering the era and my transitions from one band to another up to the present day, without going back over the data which we have, and

letting me reminisce about the different bands and musicians at leisure, I have referral notes from a great many of those incidents, and we can discuss them -- but they cannot be reinserted on the tape. Like you can in written manuscripts. You see, you can go over them and come back, and reinsert.

But tapes are a little rough in that matter, and I may miss things. I think the interest is all there, if they are added to the finished overall tapes under the heading of "Thoughts at Random", omissions and corrections and summing up of my favorite musicians I've worked with, how they enriched me musically and helped me attain the best out of my drumming, to reach peaks in my playing ability.

I have these notes to refer to, notes only, mind you -- because I might miss something very important; I might miss some very important things to me, while relating and reminiscing on tape. So if nobody has any objection, I would just love to work with you, Milt Hinton, in that manner.
As I say, I have the notes only -- I do not have a retentive memory, and I have to recall things, and the notes help me to be correct.
